reason: The cited evidence (E1, E3) supports that an equiatomic composition promotes uniform element distribution and inhibits phase separation, and that the coating forms protective oxides and increases hardness. However, the direct causal link between uniform oxide formation and improved wear performance, and the predicted degradation with compositional deviation, are not directly tested or evidenced in the cited passages.
premises: Equiatomic composition ensures homogeneous elemental distribution and inhibits phase separation
Homogeneous distribution enables a uniform protective oxide film (e.g., (Fe,Co,Ni,Mn,Cu)3O4 or Cr2O3) to form
This uniform oxide film increases hardness and provides a barrier against abrasive wear
Deviation from equiatomic composition leads to microstructural inhomogeneity and reduced oxide film quality
The equiatomic coating shows superior wear performance (low wear rate, stable friction) compared to unbalanced compositions
